newsitem.title: FRANCE: New French rulers water down military call-up plan.
newsitem.headline: New French rulers water down military call-up plan.

text.p: French Defence Minister Alain Richard said on Thursday he would scrap a controversial plan to call up young people for five days to assess their suitability for the military and to lecture them on patriotism.

Richard told reporters after a ministerial meeting that he would instead propose that all young people, including women, should be called up for a single day before their 18th birthday to learn about defence issues.

The five-day plan was a brainchild of former Defence Minister Charles Millon who wanted to keep a link between the armed forces and the public at large as France phases out compulsory national service in favour of all-professional military forces by 2002.
The Socialist government which took over after a June 1 general election regarded the five-day plan as a waste of money and initially wanted to scrap the call-up altogether.
But Richard said: "After their 18th birthday, young people who wish to do so will be able to undergo initial military training, whch would allow them to serve for some periods in reserve units."

The decision to keep a single-day programme was believed to have been made at the request of the military which, after initially opposing all such projects, began to see them as useful opportunities to interest youths in military careers.

President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist Rally For the Republic (RPR) party criticised the scrapping of the five-day plan as "both rushed and contradictory" and said the government's main motive was a desire to cut military spending.

"This is contradictory because the Socialist Party which has always fought against a professional army has shrunk away the five-day plan," said the RPR's defence expert, former minister Francois Fillon.
Jean-Marie Le Pen, leader of the far-right National Front, accused the leftist government of dismantling the French army "like previous right-wing governments."
Conscription has existed in France off-and-on since the French Revolution more than 200 years ago.
